question.text: Parallel Structure can be expensive for investors because:

answer.text: Each Offshore Fund has its own Investment Manager charging management/performance fees

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the workbook (p.78), in a parallel structure each offshore fund makes its own independent investment decisions and is serviced by its own offshore investment manager. The resulting offshore IM fee layer sits on top of the onshore fees, which is why the fee structure may be expensive compared with a master-feeder arrangement. The Trap: Fees are clearly charged, and the higher cost is driven by the extra investment-manager layer rather than paperwork volume or any LVF-specific rule. Note: Page 78 lists more than one rationale for using a parallel structure, including jurisdiction-specific tax treatment and flexibility in independent investment selection for each offshore vehicle.
